learning_outcomes.text: Identify simplified structural models, using the tools of rigid and deformable body mechanics.

Understand problems related to the equilibrium of a body, methods of analysis, and the determination of internal stress characteristics, integrated with knowledge of kinematics and the tools of structural analysis for rigid and deformable systems.
Understand the stress and strain state of a body or system of bodies in relation to the material properties derived from characterization tests such as tensile and/or surface hardness tests.
Design safe and functional medical devices, optimizing the design and improving the performance of devices through solid structural analysis.
Describe, address, and solve simple problems related to the equilibrium of isostatic, hyperstatic, or unstable systems, particularly in the context of human body kinematics.
Know and understand the basic tools of Structural Mechanics.
Apply the knowledge gained to simple solid mechanics problems with autonomy in choosing the solution methodology.
Independently research and learn solutions for problems not previously addressed or innovative, and be able to present them appropriately.

syllabus_topics: Fundamentals of Mechanics: Vector Calculus and Applied Vectors
Constraints in the plane and internal constraints
Basic Concepts: Force, Moment, Stress, Strain
Statics Laws: Equilibrium of Forces and Moments
Mechanical Properties of Materials: Elasticity, Plasticity, Tensile, Compressive, and Shear Strength
Linear Elastic Model (Hooke’s Law) and Nonlinear Materials, particularly Viscoelastic Models
Normal and Shear Stresses, Principal Stresses, and Mohr's Circles
assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test and an oral test. The written test lasts 2 hours and consists of practical exercises, graded in thirtieths. Students who obtain a grade higher than 18/30 in the written test access the oral test. The oral test involves discussion of the written test and course topics. The final grade is based on an overall evaluation of acquired skills, not an average of the two tests.
